anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly + Replication Synchronization Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : Costing inputs (row counts, histograms, correlations) are stale or incomplete, causing systematic cardinality misestimation and sub-optimal plans.
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly : Engine-level memory, I/O, parallelism, and checkpoint/redo settings are mis-tuned for the actual hardware and workload, distorting runtime behavior regardless of physical capacity.
Replication Synchronization Anomaly : Standby or downstream replicas cannot receive or apply WAL/redo as fast as the primary generates it, leading to growing replication lag and log-retention pressure.

Composite definition: The database concurrently suffers from inaccurate optimizer statistics, ill-calibrated configuration parameters, and impaired replication throughput. Together they create a multi-layer performance and availability degradation in which poor plan quality, resource misallocation, and backlog in the replication pipeline reinforce one another.

Combined anomalous phenomena: 1) Queries on the primary intermittently swing between very fast and severely slow executions, with explain plans showing grossly off row-count estimates, high memory spills, or runaway parallelism. 2) Mis-sized buffers, work-mem, or checkpoint intervals inflate redo generation and increase flush storms, amplifying log-write waits even while CPU or storage remain under-utilised. 3) Replication monitor views show widening receive/replay lag, growing retained log segments, and replicas serving progressively staler data; failovers become risky as retained logs approach disk limits. 4) After bulk loads or schema changes, statistics staleness triggers massive sequential scans whose bloated I/O, memory, and redo output collide with poorly tuned background writer and WAL parameters, further starving replication workers and extending apply latency. Symptoms cross domains, obscuring root causes: log bloat may be misattributed to storage when it is jointly driven by bad plans and sub-optimal checkpoint sizing.

Causal interaction: Stale or missing statistics generate inefficient plans (e.g., full-table scans, oversized hash aggregates) that explode I/O and redo volume. Because configuration parameters (buffer pool, work_mem, checkpoint_timeout, wal_buffers, parallelism limits) are mis-set, the engine cannot absorb the extra load, leading to more frequent checkpoints, longer log flush times, and head-of-line blocking. The surge in WAL traffic overwhelms replication channels already operating near capacity; as replicas fall behind, the primary must retain additional log segments, increasing disk pressure and further lengthening checkpoints. Elevated write and memory contention from mis-configured resources slows statistics auto-collection, perpetuating staleness and creating a reinforcing loop where each anomaly exacerbates the others, culminating in severe performance volatility, storage exhaustion risk, and degraded high-availability posture.

entry.official_definition: Specifies the amount of time after which a TCP keepalive message that has not been acknowledged by the client should be retransmitted.
entry.trigger_condition: A TCP keepalive probe is not acknowledged for tcp_keepalives_interval on systems supporting TCP_KEEPINTVL or an equivalent socket option.
entry.workload_impact: Controls retry timing for keepalive probes used to detect unresponsive client connections.
entry.default_behavior: Default value is 0, selecting the operating system default.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
